newsitem.title: CHILE: Spain's Iberia to sell Chilean airline stake.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Iberia to sell Chilean airline stake.

text.p: Spanish airline Iberia will sell its 38 percent stake in Chilean airline Ladeco to local investors who own the rest of the company, said Ladeco president Jose Cox.
"With this arrangement we will end once and for all the split within Ladeco and give the company a great opportunity to develop," Cox told a news conference.
Iberia and the airlines Chilean shareholders have been at loggerheads in recent years on the management of Ladeco, Chile's second largest national airline.
Cox declined to give details of the value of the deal, but said the sale could take place by the end of the month.
Local media have said that Iberia has agreed to sell its stake for around $8 million.
Ladeco's majority shareholders will carry out a $15 million capital increase within the next two months, said Cox.
"A very large part of the capital will be used to pay debts and, naturally, we will have to put funds aside for the partial renewal and expansion of the fleet," he said.
Ladeco was taken over in 1995 by the owners of local rival LanChile.
